extracted.intended_audience: web managers and content strategists (digital teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating public-facing government web content that is clear, audience-focused, and legally compliant with the Plain Writing Act; covers writing, content design, and user testing to ensure comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language (clarity and ease of understanding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain language – content that is clear and easy to understand – is critical to helping the public to make sense of their obligations and benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write content so the public can quickly understand obligations and benefits; prioritize clarity and ease of reading. (Page frames plain language as the central quality goal for public-facing content.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-specific writing / write for your specific audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plain Writing Act of 2010 established the requirement that content for the public is written for its specific audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the intended audience and tailor vocabulary, examples, and structure to that group's needs and background so they can understand the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of plain language
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of plain language principles, writing for your audience, and the Plain Writing Act of 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow core plain-language principles (as summarized in the linked resource) when planning and drafting content; use the principles to guide organization, tone, and word choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of how to write clear content that follows plain language guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply specific writing techniques (structure, sentence-level clarity, active voice, plain vocabulary) to make content understandable; consult the 'writing for understanding' resource for practical tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for understanding (content design supports plain language)
rubrics_metrics.description: How content design can support plain language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use content design (layout, headings, visual hierarchy, chunking, labels) to make information scannable and comprehensible; design choices should reinforce plain-language writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for understanding (user testing for comprehension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to test that your content is easily understandable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct user testing or other evaluation methods to verify that your target audience understands the content; iterate based on test findings to improve clarity and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal compliance with the Plain Writing Act of 2010
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plain Writing Act of 2010 requires that content for the public be written for its specific audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure content practices meet the statutory requirement by documenting audience analysis, applying plain-language principles, and testing content for comprehension as part of compliance efforts.
